claim: The AWS database decision guide says to choose Amazon Aurora when you are migrating or modernizing an on-premises relational workload, or when the workload has less predictable query patterns, and that Aurora supports MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible engines.
question: According to the AWS database decision guide, when do you choose Amazon Aurora?

values.display: migrating or modernizing an on-premises relational workload
values.spoken: migrating or modernizing an on-premises relational workload

qualifiers.scope: Aurora in the AWS database decision guide

note: The same row says Aurora has up to five times the throughput of standard MySQL; the Aurora overview page says up to 6x. Not recorded as a fact because the two pages disagree.
